articles.body: G7 foreign ministers will revisit Russia’s war in Ukraine and the prospect of further US strikes on Iran when they meet in Paris. Washington has kept the option of new strikes open since Republicans lost the midterm elections. Rubio is due to attend both days, compared with one in March.
articles.headline: Europe to press US on Ukraine peace and Iran at Paris G7 talks

articles.body: President Donald Trump vowed a political comeback on Sunday after Republicans lost control of Congress in last Tuesday’s midterms, as incoming Democratic leaders pledged to hold his administration to account, and the attorney general promised to defend officials against threatened prosecutions.
articles.headline: Trump vows comeback as parties clash over Democrat prosecution threats

articles.body: Nvidia’s board said Sunday it would investigate reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported Huang had an affair with an executive US intelligence believed was gathering information for Beijing. Huang will remain CEO during the inquiry and has pledged cooperation.
articles.headline: Nvidia to probe reports that Chinese intelligence targeted CEO Jensen Huang

articles.body: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Argentina on Sunday from Uruguay, where his tour began, facing calls to help bridge divisions after three years of austerity under President Javier Milei. The visit to Buenos Aires is the first by a pontiff to the late Pope Francis’ homeland in nearly four decades.
articles.headline: Pope Leo criticises Milei’s austerity in Argentina, says growth must benefit all

articles.body: Pope Leo heads to Argentina for the second leg of his South America tour, where he's expected to draw the biggest turnout of his Papacy so far. The pontiff has wrapped up his first visit to Uruguay. Colleen Dulle, Vatican Correspondent at America Magazine and the co-host of the 'Inside the Vatican' podcast, joins us to analyse the significance of his Latin American tour.
articles.headline: Pope Leo in Latin America: Papal Politics and Peru

articles.body: Israel's ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot was tapped by President Isaac Herzog to try to form a government Sunday evening. But his lack of a clear majority in parliament will make trying to forge a coalition alongside the country's divided minor parties an uphill struggle.
articles.headline: Israeli opposition leader Eisenkot begins the hard work of forging a coalition government

articles.body: A boat carrying migrants along the hazardous Atlantic Ocean route from West Africa to Europe sank off the coast of Senegal, killed at least 34 people, authorities said Sunday. Only one survivor has so far been found, and "an indeterminate number" are still missing.
articles.headline: Migrant boat sinks off Senegal, killing at least 34 people, authorities say

articles.body: Hundreds of thousands of Ukrainians were left without electricity on Sunday following Russian airstrikes targeting the country's energy infrastructure. Moscow has intensified its attacks as winter approaches, leaving residents in Kyiv and other parts of the country struggling with power cuts as temperatures continue to drop. Clemence Waller reports.
articles.headline: Ukraine: Russian strikes leave hundreds of thousands without power

articles.body: Israel's opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has officially been tasked with forming the country's next government, following a formal announcement by President Isaac Herzog. He now has up to six weeks to negotiate with potential coalition partners and secure a parliamentary majority. While an alliance with Arab Israeli parties appears to be the easiest option mathematically, it remains politically sensitive. Eisenkot must now navigate difficult negotiations to build a coalition capable of replacing Benjamin Netanyahu. Noga Tarnopolsky reports from Jerusalem.
articles.headline: Gadi Eisenkot receives mandate to form government

articles.body: Spanish tennis star Carlos Alcaraz avenged his loss to American player Ben Shelton in the US Open in September as he inched ahead of his rival Sunday to win the Paris Masters for the first time. It was Shelton's first defeat in a Masters final.
articles.headline: Spain's Alcaraz beats error-prone Shelton to win Paris Masters for first time

articles.body: From the Democratic Party's big wins in the US midterm elections to France's ongoing student-led protests and the first Olympic sports event held on African soil, FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images.
articles.headline: The week in pictures: US midterms 'Blue Wave', French protests and Dakar Youth Olympics

articles.body: In Tuesday’s US midterm elections, voters weighed in on more than 40 local measures on data centres, and sided against them in all but one. With Democrats taking control of Congress in January and new governors in Texas and Georgia calling for moratoriums, the AI building boom faces its toughest political test yet.
articles.headline: US voters reject AI data centres: could the backlash spread to France?

articles.body: One month into the Yemeni government's offensive against the Iran-aligned Houthis, fighting continues to escalate along the Red Sea coast. Meanwhile, the humanitarian crisis is worsening, with hundreds of thousands of people displaced and the country facing the threat of catastrophe. Rula Amin, Senior Communications Advisor and spokesperson at UNHCR at Amman, in Jordan, shares further details.
articles.headline: Yemen's humanitarian crisis worsens

articles.body: Poland on Sunday launched a terror probe into the mass shooting in Krakow the day before, in which six people were killed and many more were injured. Authorities have said that the 24-year-old suspect, who used a semi-automatic rifle in his killing spree, was “fascinated by far-right ideologies”. He is currently in critical condition in hospital. FRANCE 24 journalist Adrien Sariat reports from Poland.
articles.headline: Poland in shock after 6 killed in Krakow far-right shooting

articles.body: French sailor Tom Laperche has won the Route du Rhum, setting a new record in the transatlantic yacht race. The 29-year-old crossed the finish line in Guadeloupe on his first attempt, beating the previous 2022 record by around six hours. A remarkable debut in one of sailing's toughest competitions!
articles.headline: French skipper wins Route du Rhum

articles.body: Poland has launched a terrorism investigation after a deadly shooting left six people dead and 16 injured. The 24-year-old Polish suspect was reportedly fascinated by far-right ideologies. Authorities are investigating the possible extremist motive as Krakow's main square remains sealed. Two days of national mourning have been declared for the victims.
articles.headline: Mourning in Poland after mass shooting

articles.body: France will participate in the upcoming Abu Dhabi peace talks on ending the Ukraine war, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Sunday, adding that Europeans will be represented at the summit. The talks will take place under US mediation on Tuesday and Wednesday.
articles.headline: Europe will take part in US-mediated Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi, French FM says

articles.body: Pope Leo XIV urged men to respect their wives as he wrapped up the first leg of his 12-day tour of Latin America. The region recorded nearly 20,000 instances of women being killed over the past five years alone, most of them murdered by a current or former partner.
articles.headline: Pope Leo urges men to respect wives amid Latin American femicide crisis

articles.body: French police have made extensive use of tear gas during protests that have roiled France in recent weeks, sometimes causing grievous injuries. Thousands of accounts of women experiencing acutely painful periods and increased bleeding are further challenging assumptions that the chemical irritant carries only minor consequences.
articles.headline: ‘10 times more painful’: Menstrual disorders fuel calls to ban tear gas at French protests

articles.body: Senegal won two gold medals in beach wrestling at the Youth Olympic Games in Dakar. Elisabeth Diatta won gold in the -55 kg category, the host country’s first gold medal at the Youth Olympic Games. Her compatriot Maguette Diop followed suit, taking gold in the -80 kg category.
articles.headline: 2026 Dakar Youth Olympic Games: Golden Double for Senegal

articles.body: Diwali celebrations began on Sunday, with people across India and the global diaspora gathering to mark one of the most important festivals in the Hindu tradition. In Ayodhya, believed to be the birthplace of Lord Rama, the deity celebrated during the festival, festivities included performances based on the Hindu epic Ramayana, laser and light shows, live music, fireworks and drone displays.
articles.headline: Diwali: Over one billion people mark victory of light over darkness

articles.body: Paraguay's ousted president, Santiago Peña, has been charged over the collapse of Ueno Bank. Initially placed under house arrest, he has since been transferred to a military facility for his own safety. Nearly three million customers were locked out of their accounts after regulators seized control of the online bank. Repayments are now under way, but protests continue as customers demand access to their money. Peña denies any wrongdoing. Jack Pownall reports.
articles.headline: Paraguay: Senate impeached Peña rather than accept his offer to resign

articles.body: Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Sunday officially tasked ex-military chief Gadi Eisenkot with trying to form a government after neither Eisenkot's bloc nor that or incumbent Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu won a clear majority in Israel's October 27 elections. Eisenkot now has up to six weeks to form a coalition government. Follow our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.
articles.headline: Israeli president officially tasks Eisenkot with forming government

articles.body: AUSTIN, Texas — Gina Hinojosa’s stunning victory put Texas at the epicenter of a political earthquake — and the aftershocks could upend Andy Beshear’s path to the White House. For months, increasingly frustrated Hinojosa allies publicly and privately pressured the Democratic Governors Association, which Beshear chairs, to help push her over the finish line, as many national Democrats and donors stayed on the sidelines. On Tuesday, Hinojosa dominated the race for the Texas governor’s mansion, riding a blue wave that swept Democrats into power across the country, including flipping six governorships in states won by President Donald Trump. Latino operatives who spoke with POLITICO feel vindicated — and are turning their knives on Beshear ahead of a potential 2028 presidential bid. “His presidential campaign is over,” said Sergio Gonzalez, a Democratic operative working on programs to turn out Latino voters in the midterms. Beshear “doesn't understand politics in the way that a president needs to understand politics,” and “failed Latino voters and Texas voters and Democrats in this moment,” said Gonzalez, who previously worked as a top aide to former Vice President Kamala Harris’ campaign. Hinojosa’s race became the ultimate underdog campaign — a push to conquer a state Democrats had all but abandoned, with a candidate from the increasingly conservative Rio Grande Valley who her team was betting could turn out Latino voters in droves. Many national Democrats privately believed Hinojosa didn’t have a shot. But as public polling showed her closing the gap with three-term incumbent GOP Gov. Greg Abbott, the DGA’s minimal involvement in the race turned into a blistering wound that Hinojosa’s allies argued cut at the heart of the party’s historic lack of investment in Latino communities and candidates. It’s made the Texas race the heart of an intra-party debate that’s only poised to explode ahead of 2028, when Latino voters will be central to any winning presidential coalition. And her allies are out to challenge Beshear’s party leadership potential, taking their shots arguing that the Texas victory is not his to claim. “Andy Beshear is going to have to look at his playbook and understand that there was some pretty big missteps,” Stephanie Valencia, co-founder of Latino polling firm Equis Research, told POLITICO. The DGA defended its involvement and Beshear’s leadership, touting the more than $1.4 million it spent in Texas, including paying for campaign expenses and staff on the ground to support Hinojosa. The organization noted it featured Hinojosa at multiple events hosted by governors to introduce candidates like her to national donors. “We always believed in Gina and knew she could win,” Meghan Meehan-Draper, the DGA’s executive director, said in a statement. “The DGA was proud to support her campaign as its largest contributor, along with our $12 million investment in Latino outreach across multiple successful campaigns on the path to electing a majority of Democratic governors for the first time since 2010.” But Hinojosa’s allies say it was about more than just money. In its final months, the surprising viability of Hinojosa’s campaign sparked a stand-off between Latino consultants, organizations and members of Congress on one side, and the national Democratic gubernatorial campaign arm on the other, over how to invest in winning Latinos, a bloc of voters whose tendencies to swing between parties is redefining the political landscape. The campaign itself is also taking a shot at the DGA and Beshear. Hinojosa’s win “was the result of a curiosity that too many people in the establishment are still scared to embrace,” campaign manager Amy Friedman wrote in a post-election memo obtained by POLITICO. “Even the Democratic Governors Association — the entity set up to literally help Democrats win — never believed she could.” The DGA’s investments haven’t added up to any goodwill for Beshear from the Latino leaders and Hinojosa’s allies, who accuse the Kentucky governor of first ignoring and later forgoing a chance to put his full weight behind Hinojosa, who on Tuesday became the state’s first Latina governor. “Don’t even get me started,” said Rebecca Katz of Fight Agency, which worked with Gina’s campaign and has been calling out Beshear on X . “[The DGA] underestimated her every step of the way. Not only did they not give [that much] to Gina, but they actively undermined her with other donors. It was outrageous.” What Hinojosa’s campaign and allies saw as a generational opportunity to take a risk and flip Texas was met with deep skepticism and an even deeper lack of resources across an ever-growing map of competitive governor’s races in a blue wave year. Texas is among the most expensive states in the country to campaign in, and rallying donors to spend big on state-level races has long been a party problem. Abbott had a massive war chest of $105.7 million and the backing of Elon Musk, the world’s richest man, who poured nearly half a billion dollars into the midterms overall. Dozens of Latino leaders, in two separate letters from September to October, pleaded with the DGA and Beshear to invest more in Hinojosa’s bid, at first asking for $10 million and later lowering it to $3 million. The calls for a massive influx of cash that could level the playing field fell on deaf ears until the final weeks of the campaign. On Sept. 29, Beshear called Hinojosa to commit $1 million from the DGA. Playing out in the background was the looming 2028 Democratic presidential landscape, which had already shifted to heavily rely on Latino voters even before Texas entered the picture. Beshear is one of many Democrats considering a presidential run. But other potential contenders jumped in forcefully to back Hinojosa, making her campaign into a mini 2028 proxy battle. Arizona Sen. Ruben Gallego, who was among the signatories of the letters to the DGA, campaigned with her twice. Both California Gov. Gavin Newsom and Maryland Gov. Wes Moore contributed to her campaign or fundraised for her. And Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker not only helped fund the DGA itself, but separately pledged $1.2 million to Hinojosa in early October , after Beshear’s phone call with Hinojosa. “I was pleased to be able to support her,” Pritzker said in response to questions from POLITICO at a news conference Wednesday. “I think that I catalyzed others to.” Gallego told POLITICO he “believed in Gina from Day One.” While he didn’t directly level any criticism toward Beshear or the DGA, he said her campaign is a teaching moment for the road to 2028, which could see Texas newly competitive at the state and presidential level. “We need to at least learn from this that there's a lot more possibilities, that we should be looking at these states that people used to think are unreachable, and understand that if we have good talent and we have good energy, that we should make investments going forward,” Gallego said. Beshear has not shut down speculation about his presidential ambitions, and leading the DGA has afforded him the opportunity to be the front and center for some of the biggest statewide races in the country. Carlos Eduardo Espina, the popular Gen-Z Latino social media star, has appeared multiple times with Beshear this year. Espina, who emcee’d Hinojosa’s watch party, doesn’t share the same concerns as many of the Latino operatives who’ve also backed Hinojosa. Espina said he has a “great relationship” with Beshear and that the Kentucky governor has actively courted Latino support for months. “He's honestly one of the best leaders we have in our party on how to reach people and how to communicate with voters who might feel disengaged from the political process,” Espina said. Beshear pushed for the seven-figure investment that eventually landed in Texas, and “personally pushed to send more money from the DGA in the closing week,” said Eric Hyers, Beshear’s longtime ally and former campaign manager. Beshear also made a $25,000 donation from his leadership PAC and separately invested $300,000 in operations specifically targeting Latino turnout in Texas. The DGA also funneled over $12 million toward Latino outreach in Nevada and Arizona, two key presidential states with large shares of Latino voters and high-profile gubernatorial races. With several key Trump-won states in play and a wide map, and the party’s well-documented money woes, the lion’s share of the DGA’s resources went to states that looked competitive from the get-go. The goal was to “win as many races as we can,” as Beshear said to POLITICO back in September. Tuesday proved to be a massive night across the board, as the DGA flipped seats including Nevada and Democrats will now represent 30 states. “He feels good about the spending decisions that he and his colleagues made,” Hyers said of Beshear. “Under his chairmanship, all incumbent governors were reelected, every state with a Democratic governor was held — including Kansas — and Democrats flipped six states.” Yet Hinojosa’s win in Texas is the “crown jewel of the night with generational implications” when it comes to Latino voters the Democratic Party has been fighting to win back since 2024, Valencia said. The Democratic Party doesn’t need “infighting” after their blowout win, she added, but “we need to learn from our mistakes.” And even Hinojosa’s campaign points to that split of investments in calling out the DGA, with Friedman, her campaign manager, writing in the memo that “when pushed for more investment, they balked. They would go on to send six times the investment in Alaska than Texas.” Hinojosa’s upset in Texas instead came from a relentless focus on affordability issues — especially slamming the growing cost of data centers — and a historic Democratic ticket that also saw James Talarico beat Republican state Attorney General Ken Paxton in the Senate race. In a blistering midterm environment for the GOP, Hinojosa and Talarico swung historically red counties and the Latino-dominated Rio Grande Valley. It was ground zero for what became an “earthquake” of Latinos swinging en masse for Democrats across the country. Latinos haven’t felt like they have a political home, said SOMOS PAC’s Melissa Morales. Part of that comes from a lack of prioritizing the bloc and a lack of investment. The “starkest example” is Texas, she said. The criticism isn’t stopping Beshear’s team from touting his strength should he enter a presidential primary. Going into 2028, “there will now be a Democratic governor in every battleground state because Gov. Beshear and the DGA just re-wrote the 2028 map,” Hyers said. Taking the stage after her ground-shaking win in Austin, Hinojosa in one sentence touched on what had become a central intra-party tension bubbling under the surface of her meteoric rise. “It never bothered me that they doubted me — it bothered me that they doubted us,” Hinojosa told the packed room. Shia Kapos contributed to this report.
articles.headline: How Hinojosa’s win in Texas could bite Beshear

articles.body: The blue wave crashed through statehouses across the country Tuesday — carrying political and policy ramifications that will reverberate for years. Democrats flipped more than 500 state legislative seats and won control of at least a dozen legislative chambers, establishing new governing trifectas in Michigan, Arizona, Pennsylvania, Minnesota, Wisconsin and Nevada. They captured legislative chambers in Texas, Georgia and North Carolina — states long dominated by Republican lawmakers. And they picked up even more legislative seats in deep blue strongholds like New York, California and Illinois. The victories give Democrats an opening to pursue long-stalled agendas on housing costs and public education, along with new leverage in fights over taxing wealthy people and corporations and regulating artificial intelligence. Their gains will also reshape the country’s redistricting wars — and test whether Democrats can turn their backlash-fueled victories into changes voters can feel in their daily lives. “We had a generational opportunity to shift the power in our states and to affect change and we did just that,” Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee President Heather Williams said. “ We ran the table. It's amazing.” The scale of the victory is historic. In New York, Democrats are on track for their biggest state Senate majority since 1846, when they were running against the Whigs. In Texas, they won the state House for the first time since 2002. Arizona will have its first Democratic trifecta since the 1960s. And Democrats flipped Georgia's House, the first chamber Democrats have taken back in the Deep South in the modern era. Altogether, the party won more seats than in any year since the post-Watergate campaign of 1974. The gains represent the most seismic change in state capitals since Republicans shellacked Democrats nationwide in 2010, picking up nearly 700 state legislative seats and flipping 20 chambers. They used that power in the ensuing years to entrench conservative policies and redraw legislative maps in their favor in wide swaths of the country. Wisconsin Republicans, for example, swept every statewide office and won control of both legislative chambers that year, clearing the way to enact a far-reaching conservative agenda that remade the state over the ensuing decade. On Tuesday, Democrats flipped both legislative chambers. “This is an incredible moment for the state of Wisconsin and the country,” said Wisconsin Assembly Minority Leader Greta Neubauer, who’s expected to become speaker next year. ”We are going to use this power to deliver for the people of our state and demonstrate that government can be a force for good in their lives and things are different when Democrats are in charge.” Democrats have been steadily clawing their way back to power in state capitals in recent election cycles, including picking up 31 seats in special elections and Virginia’s 2025 legislative elections after Donald Trump returned to the White House. After Tuesday, they now control a narrow majority of at least 51 state legislative chambers, up from 29 when Trump first took office in 2016, according to the DLCC. But newly empowered Democratic state lawmakers will face a challenging political and economic landscape with voters angry at elected officials of all partisan stripes as they face pocketbook woes and government failings. Veteran Minnesota Republican strategist Gregg Peppin, who worked on state Senate races this cycle, said the results there largely hinged on what voters were most angry about: the state’s massive fraud scandals under Democratic governance, or a deeply unpopular president. Ultimately, Democrats padded their state Senate majority by five seats and won control of the House. “Clearly we found out they were more fed up with Donald Trump than they were with fraud,” Peppin said. “Everybody’s just worn out from the guy, I think Republicans too. It’s just time to turn the page.” In Arizona, Rep. Oscar De Los Santos, who’s poised to become speaker of the House when lawmakers reconvene in Phoenix next year, said they have a robust agenda planned given their long time in the political wilderness. “We have sixty years of pent-up ideas that we have not been able to move,” he said. “There's a bunch of legislation that we've got ready to go.” Among the items on the agenda: banning corporate landlords from buying homes, cracking down on surveillance pricing based on people’s past purchases and addressing the state’s massive water woes. De Los Santos said Democrats would crack down on Saudi-owned farms using Arizona water to grow alfalfa for export. Another top target: reigning in the state’s universal education voucher program, which allows families to tap taxpayer dollars not only for private school tuition, but also for other education-related expenses. De Los Santos points out that public dollars have been used to pay for ski trips , kitchen remodels and even lingerie . “It’s insane. It is out of control,” he said. “You've got literally thousands of dollars spent at Victoria's Secret from this program and so we're going to put an end to all of that nonsense and redirect those funds to our public schools.” Democrats also juiced their majorities Tuesday in states where they already enjoyed governing trifectas. Republicans took a beating, for example, in Chicago’s suburbs, with Democrats flipping a string of state legislative seats — held by both moderates and conservatives — and further shrinking the GOP’s once-formidable presence in the region. Republicans lost at least eight seats in the Illinois General Assembly, including six held by sitting lawmakers and two open seats. The drubbing further expands Democrats’ supermajorities in both chambers: They’ll now hold 84 out of 118 seats in the House and 45 out of 59 seats in the Senate. “It means Democrats don’t have to try to work toward the middle [on legislation], which is really where the vast majority of the electorate is,” said state GOP Rep. Dan Ugaste, who represents Chicago’s far western suburbs and was among the Republicans who lost Tuesday. Ugaste attributed the GOP losses, in part, to “many more” Democrats turning out than they did in the 2022 midterms. He also pointed to frustration with the economy and unmet expectations from the Trump administration. “The administration said on day one that they were going to improve everyone's economic situation,” Ugaste said. “And while the macro economy — businesses have orders, everyone's still employed — is at a good place, what’s hurting is whether people can afford what’s on the shelf.” In California and New York, Democrats are also poised to significantly expand their already dominant legislative majorities. In Sacramento, they control 75% of seats in the state Assembly, but with votes still being tallied they’re expected to pad that majority by at least four more seats. In New York, Democrats are poised to win at least 14 additional seats, giving them control of 158 out of 213. There’s even early speculation that — when the final results are tabulated and the electoral dust settles — that there might now be sufficient support in state legislatures to implement a presidential election system based on the popular vote. The wins also put Democratic state lawmakers in a position to help define the party’s agenda heading into 2028. “[We] need to begin to show everyone what Democrats are made of and what we're able to accomplish and how we lead,” said the DLCC’s Williams. “But also we're doing that in the context of what is expected to be a critically important and incredibly robust Democratic primary, where voters around the country are going to be able to put their mark on who the leader of the Democratic Party is going to be and where we go.” Shia Kapos contributed to this report

articles.body: Kevin Stitt, the outgoing Republican governor of Oklahoma, has a message for President Donald Trump: Try being nice. “People are just kind of tired,” Stitt told POLITICO in an interview Friday morning, three days after the Republican Party suffered devastating election losses across the country and a few hours before Trump elevated Stephen Miller to be his chief of staff. “They are just ready for something new and a change ... President Trump’s policies are amazing, and he does a really good job on a lot of fronts, but the civility and then just trying to be nice to people, I think would go a long way.” Stitt, who was until this summer chair of the National Governors Association, has been in Trump’s crosshairs before. In February, Trump lashed out at Stitt in a dispute over the annual NGA gathering at the White House, calling the Oklahoma governor a “ RINO ” and a “ wiseguy .” The two later appeared to patch things up , after a White House sit-down in March. Stitt is now one of several prominent Republicans calling on the president and congressional leaders to take stock of the party’s midterm losses and change course heading into 2028. Asked on Friday if Trump had been nice to him, Stitt laughed, before replying: “I’ve always gotten along with President Trump. He’s always been good to me.” But the term-limited governor, who has said he intends to return to the private sector next year, did not shy away from calling out the president. Stitt urged Trump to stop directing the Department of Justice to go after his political opponents — tactics the governor described as “Third World country stuff” — and use his final two years in the White House to seriously pursue bipartisan immigration reform. This transcript has been edited for length and clarity. You called last year’s election results a “ butt whipping ” for the party. If 2025 was a butt whipping, what was 2026? Oh man! I don't swear, but it's probably worse than a butt whipping. It was pretty bad. But here's the deal: I think it didn't go the way that we had hoped, but I just want everybody to know, it's not the end of the world. We're all Americans, and it really shows you that we're not as partisan as we think. In other words, the American people can swing both directions, right? That’s a positive. Our leadership matters, the way we conduct ourselves matters. The American people wanted something different, and I think in two years we'll see what happens. I think [Texas Gov. Greg] Abbott's loss was really the most shocking to me because he's such a good guy and has been a great governor for Texas, and I don't think anybody saw that coming. What happened? Why do you think the results went the way they did? People are tired of the self-dealing that they see in politicians. They see people going to Congress and getting rich, and government contracts to big business. I think people are just really, really cranky right now. Obviously, the kitchen table issues like diesel prices are super hard on the average American, and things are costing more, and I think people are frustrated. We've got to get back to talking about spending. The national debt [is] out of control. We're spending $2 trillion. It doesn't matter if Republicans or Democrats are in office. People don't even talk about tax policy anymore because they think they can spend whatever they want, regardless of income, and that is driving things up. We have got to have permitting reform done. If you think about why are gas prices so expensive, part of that you could blame on the war in Iran, but a lot of it is the lack of development of new gas processing pipelines. It takes us eight years to build things anymore, and we have so squashed the private sector from meeting the needs of Americans through over-regulation. Do Republicans need to do a better job of messaging? They need to do a better job of messaging. But they also need to do a better job of leading when we get there. I think the American people are so tired of weaponizing the Department of Justice. When President [Joe] Biden, his party was raiding Mar-a-Lago, they were suing President Trump, and then Trump wins big. I wish that we wouldn't have flipped the script and started weaponizing and going after political opponents. This is Third World country stuff. We have got to stop that. Now, when the Democrats are in power, if they try to start impeaching Trump again and try weaponizing and investigating instead of leading, I think the American people are going to be frustrated in two years again. How much blame do you place on President Trump for the midterm results? President Trump is what he is… I think just over 10 years, people are just kind of tired. They're just ready for something new and a change. President Trump's policies are amazing, and he does a really good job on a lot of fronts. But the civility and just kind of being nice to people, I think would go a long way. Has Trump been nice to you? I have always gotten along with President Trump. He has always been good to me. But you know … we all know that the president, he's a fighter, and it's so tough to be the president because everybody's always attacking him. But I think that just a little more decorum, and people would give him more of the benefit of the doubt. He is talking now about potentially working across the aisle . I know you brought up permitting reform. Are there other areas where you would like to see him and the administration working with Democrats on Capitol Hill? Immigration reform is something where I think there's a really good opportunity. President Trump is the president that has the credibility because he secured the borders after Biden's disaster, and literally he could be the one that could really give us some immigration policy that allows the workforce that we need. Do you see the midterm results as a response to the administration’s immigration enforcement tactics? Was this a rejection of the way that immigration has been handled? That may be just one part of it, but it is certainly more nuanced than that. I think it is just an overall frustration with the party that's in charge right now, and the people are wanting something different. If there's violent criminals, we need them out. But there was a case in Oklahoma where the guy had been here since he was eight years old from Vietnam, and he worked for a company, the company was vouching for him ... but he had a marijuana charge from 20 years ago that was expunged by the state when he was in college. But yet he's been deported, has a wife and two kids. That’s the kind of thing that doesn't make sense to the average person. And that's where people are like, “Hey, we're all for getting violent criminals out, but this guy is chasing the American dream, contributing. He is one that we should give a workforce permit to. Where do you think the Republican Party needs to go from here?  The American people are looking for civility. They are looking for a statesman. They are looking for someone that is not as partisan that is saying, “Hey, we're all Americans. Well, we can disagree better. We can disagree with one another on policy, but let's start debating the policy, like our founders talked about.”

articles.body: <p> A tres semanas para que se abran las urnas en España, la ventaja del bloque de la derecha se muestra inalterable. La suma del PP, Vox y UPN en las elecciones generales del próximo día 29 reuniría la mitad de los votos emitidos y rebasaría los 190 escaños, más de 15 por encima de la mayoría absoluta del Congreso, según la última encuesta de 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la SER. La mayor incertidumbre en estos momentos reside en quién será el más votado de entre los dos grandes partidos, ya que la diferencia entre PP y PSOE se ha acortado a dos puntos, dentro del margen de error del sondeo. Los socialistas experimentan un importante avance, pese <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/accidente-ferrocarriles-urda-2026/" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/accidente-ferrocarriles-urda-2026/">a la catástrofe ferroviaria de Urda</a>, mientras los grupos a su izquierda se sitúan bajo mínimos. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-09/el-bloque-de-la-derecha-mantiene-su-ventaja-pero-el-psoe-se-acerca-al-pp.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/motivos-y-riesgos-de-una-huelga-general-atipica-que-pretende-marcar-un-antes-y-un-despues.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/motivos-y-riesgos-de-una-huelga-general-atipica-que-pretende-marcar-un-antes-y-un-despues.html">La huelga general</a> convocada por los sindicatos para el próximo miércoles día 11, con la vivienda como reivindicación principal, divide casi en dos mitades a los españoles. La apoyan un 46,3% y la rechazan algunos más, el 48,8%, según una encuesta de 40dB. para EL PAÍS y la SER. La posición crítica con esos movimientos sociales crece un poco más en el caso de las acampadas, que las reprueban un 53% de los encuestados. Las medidas y decretos aprobados por el Gobierno para intentar atajar la carestía de la vivienda —el último paquete será probablemente aprobado este jueves <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/el-pnv-volvera-a-apoyar-el-decreto-principal-de-vivienda.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-06/el-pnv-volvera-a-apoyar-el-decreto-principal-de-vivienda.html">por la Diputación Permanente del </a>Congreso— despiertan escaso entusiasmo: apenas uno de cada cuatro entrevistados valoran su eficacia. Los microdatos de la encuesta, que también incluyen intención de voto, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-09/consulte-todos-los-datos-internos-del-sondeo-preelectoral-de-el-pais-cuestionarios-cruces-y-respuestas-individuales.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-09/consulte-todos-los-datos-internos-del-sondeo-preelectoral-de-el-pais-cuestionarios-cruces-y-respuestas-individuales.html">pueden consultarse en las webs de ambos medios</a>.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-11-09/la-huelga-divide-a-los-espanoles-y-mas-de-la-mitad-rechaza-las-acampadas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>A medida que se acerca la fecha de la huelga general, los sindicatos han nutrido de razones y contenidos la convocatoria que nació del Sindicato de Inquilinas, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-07/muere-maricarmen-la-mujer-que-encendio-la-lucha-contra-los-desahucios-en-espana.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-07/muere-maricarmen-la-mujer-que-encendio-la-lucha-contra-los-desahucios-en-espana.html">tras el fallecimiento de Maricarmen Abascal</a>, desahuciada de su hogar. articles.body: <img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/QAP5WUDRJRCVFGE2MXBJAEE65E.jpg?auth=5da28bc9a5f4379193da6622f7f094f9185310b8360048118beca6a57d002584" width="5000" height="3335" alt="El piloto Jesús Mateos, la médico Almudena Moreno y el mecánico Lukasz Barszczyk, el miércoles en el helipuerto del Hospital Nacional de Parapléjicos de Toledo."></img><p>Les llaman <i>Los Gigantes,</i> por los molinos de viento que hizo inmortales Miguel de Cervantes y por la misión quijotesca que libran salvando vidas a diario en las distancias infinitas de Castilla-La Mancha, la tercera comunidad más extensa de España. Muchas veces en medio de la nada, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-05/las-vidas-que-se-pararon-para-siempre-en-urda.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-05/las-vidas-que-se-pararon-para-siempre-en-urda.html">como en el accidente ferroviario de Urda</a>. La capacidad de los servicios de emergencia de la Junta para hacer transfusiones de sangre en sus cuatro helicópteros sanitarios pudo evitar que la cifra de 69 fallecidos por la colisión del AVE con el Iryo fuese mayor. De los 110 heridos que fueron hospitalizados en seis hospitales de la región, solo falleció una persona. “Se hicieron transfusiones sobre el terreno a ocho pacientes. Les ganamos tiempo. Cada minuto que se retrasa la transfusión a un paciente que la necesita aumenta un 5% las posibilidades de que fallezca. Muy probablemente alguno lo hubiera hecho”, explica Alberto López, de 48 años y director de la Gerencia de Urgencias, Emergencias y Transporte Sanitario del Servicio de Salud de Castilla-La Mancha (Sescam). </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-09/los-helicopteros-pioneros-que-salvaron-vidas-en-el-accidente-de-urda-perdimos-la-cuenta-de-la-gente-a-la-que-llegamos-a-atender.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/VFSCV25IQBFWVNJX525R5NIHPM.jpg?auth=dcbbd036f1c5b5b6f1a490be19b56833a5dd59ba8a61fb52feb951ea28c4f107" width="5000" height="3335" alt="Jesús Mateos, delante del helicóptero sanitario Eco Charlie 135 que pilota en los servicios de emergencia de Castilla-La Mancha. "></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/4RS7QO4BJJGFPEPZLUINQDBYZE.jpg?auth=916542a2c06e992b4e7f2e5a6cdb57e0d7467502b48447e8c9009351da4fd8e0" width="5000" height="3335" alt="Almudena Moreno, médico que participó en las labores de rescate tras el accidente de Urda."></img><img src="https://imagenes.elpais.com/resizer/v2/3L3G4XCNONEYHNOR6Q7P25K6AA.jpg?auth=f81973daa8311c28dac44ea0d88f3d3d8c3635b179b273e42fadf6b2edd6fb89" width="5000" height="3335" alt="Jesús Mateos, Almudena Moreno y Lukasz Barszczyk, en la base de helicópteros sanitarios de Toledo."></img>

articles.body: <p>Los dos grandes cuarteles generales de la política española, el del PP y el PSOE, tienen una enorme diferencia de enfoque en un tema central: la política internacional. En el PP creen que prácticamente nadie en España va a votar mirando a lo que pasa fuera. Están convencidos, según explican varios de sus miembros, de que las elecciones se deciden en asuntos puramente españoles o con claro componente local: el <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-11-30/el-antisanchismo-esta-de-fiesta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2024-11-30/el-antisanchismo-esta-de-fiesta.html">antisanchismo</a>, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-06-21/el-trio-koldoabaloscerdan-se-rompe-entre-reproches-de-grave-corrupcion.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2025-06-21/el-trio-koldoabaloscerdan-se-rompe-entre-reproches-de-grave-corrupcion.html">la corrupción,</a> <a href="https://www.bing.com/search?q=crisis+de+ceuta+site%3Aelpais.com&cvid=073a5e4e63d449349b8f0a8541b949db&gs_lcrp=EgRlZGdlKgYIABBFGDkyBggAEEUYOTIICAEQ6QcY_FXSAQgzODU3ajBqNKgCALACAA&FORM=ANAB01&PC=U531" target="_self" rel="" title="https://www.bing.com/search?q=crisis+de+ceuta+site%3Aelpais.com&cvid=073a5e4e63d449349b8f0a8541b949db&gs_lcrp=EgRlZGdlKgYIABBFGDkyBggAEEUYOTIICAEQ6QcY_FXSAQgzODU3ajBqNKgCALACAA&FORM=ANAB01&PC=U531">Ceuta</a>, <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-31/ultima-hora-y-reacciones-tras-el-accidente-de-trenes-de-urda-toledo-en-directo.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-31/ultima-hora-y-reacciones-tras-el-accidente-de-trenes-de-urda-toledo-en-directo.html">el accidente de Urda,</a> la amnistía, el nacionalismo, Bildu, la inmigración, la okupación. Su líder, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, apenas habla de asuntos internacionales y no se mueve cómodo ahí. Pero el PP no parece preocupado por esa cuestión. “Ahí no se juegan las elecciones”, insisten. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-11-08/sanchez-se-sube-a-la-ola-de-resistencia-progresista-americana.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: <p>El primer lunes tras el accidente de Urda (Toledo), Iván Redondo, ex jefe de gabinete de Pedro Sánchez, echaba la bola a rodar al proponer la “renacionalización” del ferrocarril español. Más de un millón de visualizaciones, seis mil comentarios a la propuesta <a href="https://x.com/thewarroomblog/status/2117157222929027273" target="_self" rel="" title="https://x.com/thewarroomblog/status/2117157222929027273">resumida en un post</a> y los partidos a la izquierda del PSOE la hacen suya. La <a href="https://cincodias.elpais.com/opinion/2026-11-06/liberalizar-no-es-privatizar.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://cincodias.elpais.com/opinion/2026-11-06/liberalizar-no-es-privatizar.html">liberalización </a>del sector ferroviario español se muestra como responsable de las 115 muertes en la alta velocidad en 2026. Pero los expertos consultados discrepan en que haya relación entre seguridad y propiedad de los trenes, con accidentes muy graves bajo modelos diversos. Los datos tampoco avalan que la red esté saturada, ni que pasen más trenes de los que pueda soportar. Pero el diseño español ha sido un tsunami para la infraestructura que Adif no ha sabido desaguar.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/economia/2026-11-08/liberalizacion-ferroviaria-un-sistema-perfecto-sobre-el-papel-que-el-gestor-no-ha-sabido-digerir.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

articles.body: La COP31 arrenca amb el repte d’abordar, teòricament, el repte de l’ electrificació . I és teòric perquè, sobre la taula, la presidència de la cimera —compartida entre Turquia i Austràlia— proposa que el 2035 l’electrificació mundial sigui del 35 % . Ara bé, de moment no consta com es concretarà això a la pràctica. També et pot interessar COP30: els reptes d’una cimera clau per al clima, amb un absent molt influent Lluís Cruz Berasategui 3 minuts de lectura Un dubte raonable Parlem d’ electrificació quan ens referim al procés pel qual se substitueixen les fonts d’energia basades en combustibles fòssils —com el petroli, el carbó i el gas natural— per electricitat, preferiblement generada a partir de fonts d’ energia renovables , com la solar, l’eòlica i la hidràulica. I és aquí on apareixen els dubtes: l’electricitat amb què es vol alimentar el 35 % d’allò que, mundialment, calgui electrificar serà d’origen renovable o fòssil? La investigadora de l’Observatori del Deute en la Globalització (ODG) Claudia Custodio explica que pot existir la temptació de “seguir generant electricitat amb la combustió de gas o de carbó “. Més, si tenim en compte, recorda Custodio, que “Turquia i Austràlia tenen reserves de carbó”. Amb tot, el gran repte que té l’ electrificació és mineral . Partint de la base que l’origen de l’electricitat amb què funcioni allò electrificat sigui renovable, la pedra a la sabata és en les bateries . Aquests dispositius d’emmagatzematge d’energia estan fabricats amb liti , cobalt i les anomenades terres rares . Són minerals que s’obtenen de l’ explotació de les mines , una indústria “amb molt impacte i petjada ecològics “, assenyala Custodio. L’ús dels combustibles fòssils és la causa de l’escalfament del planeta Un bri d’esperança La COP31 d’enguany es troba amb un calendari global col·locat en un marc geopolític diferent del de l’edició de l’any anterior, tot just una setmana després de les midterms dels Estats Units i dues setmanes després de la segona volta de les presidencials del Brasil . En aquestes cites amb les urnes, en tots dos països, els electors han barrat l’accés de l’extrema dreta negacionista del clima a les institucions, una circumstància que per la investigadora de l’ODG “és bona perquè dona un missatge al món ” en la lluita contra el canvi climàtic . Amb tot, Claudia Custodio assenyala que “la presidència brasilera de la COP30 no ha entregat fins a última hora el full de ruta —un compromís adquirit en la cimera celebrada al Brasil l’any passat — sobre com abordar la fi de l’ús dels combustibles fòssils “. També et pot interessar Barcelona impulsa l’acció climàtica en una cimera internacional a París Redacció 2 minuts de lectura El límit dels 1,5 ºC Més enllà dels aspectes concrets que marquen cada edició de les cimeres del clima, totes tenen el mateix objectiu: evitar l’escalfament global. Entitats com l’ ODG i Greenpeace han estat clares a l’hora d’ exigir a la presidència de la COP31 d’enguany —se celebrarà a la ciutat turca d’Antaya, del 9 al 20 de novembre— “un últim avís per no sobrepassar l’1,5 ºC ” de la temperatura global . En aquest sentit, bona part de les entitats no governamentals ja han reclamat un acord ferm que posi fre a la dependència dels combustibles fòssils . També et pot interessar L’acord de París, “un pas endavant, però insuficient” Sílvia Gutiérrez 1 minut de lectura

articles.body: La previsió del temps per a aquest dilluns, 9 de novembre, portarà més núvol i algun plugim a la tarda. Tot i això, la temperatura màxima es mantindrà prop dels 20ºC durant bona part del dia. Previsió horària per a Barcelona : 6 h: cel ennuvolat i temperatura d’uns 15ºC 9 h: núvols i temperatura creixent 12 h: cel ennuvolat i ambient proper a 20 ºC 15 h: començaran a caure alguns plugims 18 h: cel ennuvolat 21 h: nit tapada També et pot interessar Bruna ens portarà l’estiuet de Sant Martí: la setmana entrant començarà amb un ambient ben suau Jordi Montserrat 2 minuts de lectura Dia tapat però amb pocs canvis en la temperatura La borrasca Bruna , situada a l’oest peninsular, ens portarà una banda de núvols baixos i mitjans que cobrirà el cel durant el dia. Tot i això, el vent del sud , provocat per la combinació de la borrasca i de l’anticicló situat als Balcans, mantindrà la temperatura estable dels darrers dies. La mínima quedarà entre els 13 i 16 ºC i la màxima podrien sovintejar, de nou, la xifra dels 20 ºC. La pluja es concentrarà sobretot al oest i sud-oest de Catalunya, on serà constant però no es preveuen grans intensitats. Cap al migdia els núvols mitjans estratiformes aniran guanyant terreny al litoral i prelitoral i a primera hora de la tarda cauran alguns plugims a Barcelona i rodalia. També et pot interessar Adam, Kevin, Lola i Vera: els noms de les borrasques i danes 2026-2027 Ariadna Corominas del Hoyo 2 minuts de lectura La setmana, marcada per la suavitat: arriba l’estiuet de Sant Martí Tot i la pluja d’aquest dilluns, dimarts s’espera un repunt de la temperatura i un cel variable al llarg del dia. De cara a dimecres, Sant Martí , es preveu un dia, tal com diu la llegenda , amb una temperatura elevada que podria assolir en alguns punts els 22 ºC i un cel variable com els darrers dies. Tot i la incertesa, sembla que dijous la inestabilitat podria accentuar-se, amb una tongada de ruixats i xàfecs al litoral i prelitoral . articles.body: Ensurt majúscul a la ronda de Dalt aquest diumenge a la tarda. La via ha quedat tallada durant una estona en sentit Besòs després que s’hagi produït una persecució entre un cotxe i un vehicle de la Guàrdia Urbana . Segons ha explicat a betevé un testimoni dels fets, el vehicle que fugia de la policia ha col·lidit amb un vehicle primer i després amb un altre cotxe blanc, que ha bolcat . Aquest mateix testimoni relata que en el cotxe bolcat hi viatjaven dues noies i un noi que han pogut sortir del vehicle sense ajuda. L’accident s’ha produït entre les entrades 2 i 1 de la ronda en sentit Besòs. El vehicle que ha provocat l’accident ha fugit i ha abandonat la ronda en direcció a Santa Coloma. Fins al lloc de l’accident s’hi han desplaçat efectius del Sistema d’Emergències Mèdiques (SEM) i dels Bombers de Barcelona. Set quilòmetres de cua per sortir de Barcelona Arran de l’accident, la Guàrdia Urbana ha tallat dos carrils de circulació de la ronda de Dalt en sentit Besòs al punt quilomètric 15,5, a l’altura de Nou Barris, per poder retirar el vehicle accidentat . També s’han tallat les entrades 2 i 3 d’aquesta via. A causa del tall hi ha hagut retencions de fins a set quilòmetres en aquest punt per sortir de Barcelona. Una estona més tard, però, s’ha pogut reobrir la via i s’ha normalitzat la circulació. #GUBBarcelona Tallada la Ronda de Dalt ( #B20 ) en sentit Besos a causa d'un accident, 15,5 Km (Nou Barris). #infotrànsit pic.twitter.com/20j3IY1Ans — Ajuntament de Barcelona (@bcn_ajuntament) November 8, 2026 També et pot interessar Ets testimoni d’un accident avui? articles.body: El Barça Atlètic s’ha imposat per 3 a 0 davant el Manresa . El conjunt blaugrana ha encarrilat ràpidament el partit amb dos gols en 10 minuts. Orian Goren ha fet el primer i Pedro Rodríguez , de penal, el segon. Els locals, després d’una mala primera meitat, han estat més protagonistes al segon temps, però Álex González ha sentenciat a l’últim minut. Amb la victòria, els de Juliano Belletti segueixen, una jornada més, com a líders de la Segona Federació . El Barça Atlètic s’avança aviat en el marcador El conjunt de Juliano Belletti ha inaugurat el marcador quan només havien passat tres minuts de partit. Orian Goren ha aprofitat una centrada de Guillem Víctor per fer el primer gol de l’enfrontament (0-1). El segon ha arribat pocs minuts després, quan l’àrbitre ha assenyalat un penal molt protestat a favor dels culers. Pedro Rodríguez , amb sang freda, ha estat l’encarregat d’executar-lo per fer el segon, enganyant al porter (0-2). El conjunt manresà ha tingut l’oportunitat de retallar distàncies amb un xut de David Momoh . La rematada, des de l’àrea petita, ha sortit fregant el pal dret de la porteria d ‘Iker Rodríguez . Álex González sentencia el partit A la segona part, el Manresa ha dominat l’esfèrica. El conjunt de Sergi Trullàs ha intentat enganxar-se al partit. Carlos Portero ho ha provat des de lluny i Guzmán ha tingut l’ocasió més clara per als locals amb una rematada completament sol que ha acabat a les mans d’ Iker Rodríguez . Els manresans, tret d’una pilota al pal de Gómez al final, s’han anat desinflant i el Barça Atlètic ha sentenciat amb un gol d’ Álex González a l’últim minut. La nota negativa per als blaugrana ha estat la lesió de Caicedo . També et pot interessar Per què l’afició del Barça no volia que Marta Torrejón jugués contra el Madrid CFF? 1 minut de lectura

articles.body: Maniobra d’urgència aquest diumenge al migdia a l’ aeroport del Prat . Un vol procedent de Casablanca i amb destinació a Istanbul ha demanat desviar-se d’urgència a Barcelona per poder assistir un bebè amb problemes mèdics . Segons han explicat els controladors aeris en un missatge a X, l’infant necessitava atenció urgent i per aquest motiu s’ha facilitat un aterratge d’emergència a l’avió. Des de l’aeroport de Barcelona han coordinat l’operació perquè el vol pogués aterrar a la pista 24 esquerra, la més propera al mar i que s’utilitza per a enlairaments. També s’ha valorat que l’aparell pogués aterrar tenint en compte el pes del combustible que transportava. Un cop feta la maniobra s’han aturat els enlairaments i també s’han fet esperar momentàniament els aterratges. D’aquesta manera, des de l’aeroport s’ha pogut indicar a l’aparell que estacionés a la sortida de la pista per facilitar que els serveis mèdics poguessin arribar ràpidament a l’avió i evacuar l’infant . articles.body: El Barça ha sumat tres punts més a la Lliga per seguir líder. Golejada per 5 a 1 contra el Madrid CFF en un partit al Johan Cruyff especial per a Marta Torrejón . La defensa i llegenda blaugrana ha arribat a la xifra de 500 enfrontaments amb el Barça . L’afició no volia que jugués en aquest matx contra el conjunt madrileny perquè els agradava la idea que Torrejón complís els 500 partits dijous, 12 de novembre, al Camp Nou , en el duel de Champions contra l’Arsenal . Els culers li han fet una gran ovació quan ha entrat al terreny de joc a la segona part. El partit l’han resolt gràcies als gols d’ Esmee Brugts, Ewa Pajor, Carla Julià, Patri Guijarro i Claudia Pina . A punt de superar Alexia Putellas i Melanie Serrano Marta Torrejón és la tercera jugadora amb més partits en la història del Barça . El rècord el té Melanie Serrano amb 520 i la segueix Alexia Putellas amb 508. Fa 13 anys que Torrejón vesteix la samarreta blaugrana, en un període de gran creixement i èxit en què han guanyat 10 Lligues , nou Copes de la Reina , sis Supercopes d’Espanya i quatre Champions . La defensa de Mataró ha viscut des de dins la professionalització del Barça, des de jugar en camps de terra fins a alçar una Champions . Amb 36 anys, aquesta podria ser la seva última temporada com a jugadora professional i com a jugadora blaugrana. articles.body: Joan Laporta ha parlat en la prèvia del transcendental partit entre Atlètic de Madrid i Barça , aquest diumenge (21 h) al Metropolitano. El president blaugrana, que va viure un estiu de discordances amb el club matalasser en l’intent de fitxar Julián Álvarez , ha assegurat que ja han oblidat l’afer: “ Les relacions són molt bones , tant personalment com institucionalment. Van viure un moment difícil a l’estiu, però hi ha bona relació i l’afecte és mutu. El tema està aclarit “. Laporta, encantat amb Raphinha El president del Barça també ha destacat la figura de Raphinha . El capità blaugrana, renovat aquesta mateixa setmana fins al 2030 , és “ el millor jugador del món a la seva posició “, segons el màxim mandatari del club. Laporta ha afegit que el brasiler és un jugador molt complet, que no només juga de 9, ja que també ho pot fer en qualsevol posició de l’atac. articles.body: (ACN) Barcelona afronta aquesta setmana dies de mobilitzacions laborals a les portes de l’inici de la campanya de les eleccions espanyoles del 29-N . La vaga general de l’11 de novembre, convocada pels sindicats de treball i organitzacions com el Sindicat de Llogateres per reclamar sous i habitatges dignes, anirà precedida per protestes en altres sectors. Els treballadors de la indústria càrnia estan cridats a mobilitzar-se cinc dies a partir de dilluns; i els maquinistes de Renfe tenen plantejades aturades dimarts i dijous , el dia previ i posterior a la vaga general, per reclamar més seguretat ferroviària . En canvi, s’han cancel·lat les aturades previstes pels maquinistes d’Ouigo de dilluns. També et pot interessar Drets i deures dels treballadors per la vaga de l’11 de novembre: sou, serveis mínims i piquets Clara Aliaguilla 2 minuts de lectura Quan es fa i què reclama cada aturada? Habitatge (11 de novembre) La vaga general de dimecres és la primera de 24 hores que els sindicats majoritaris convoquen a l’estat des de la reforma laboral del PP del 2012 . Amb el lema “ Salaris. Habitatge. Preus “, l’aturada prevista per a dimecres, 11 de novembre, es fa per exigir millores salarials i d’ accés a l’habitatge , que consideren que s’ha convertit en un “factor d’empobriment i precarització laboral”. Situen com a prioritats la baixada dels preus dels lloguers , la prohibició de les compres especulatives, garantir contractes de lloguer indefinits i la suspensió dels desnonaments “sense alternativa residencial”. En l’àmbit laboral, demanen reduir la jornada a 35 hores i prohibir les hores extra estructurals, així com augments del salari mínim interprofessional (SMI) a 1.500 € i vincular els sous a la inflació. Com és habitual en aquest tipus de mobilitzacions, es preveu que incideixi molt en la mobilitat , amb possibles talls de carreteres o piquets informatius a les portes de grans indústries o empreses. Es preveuen mobilitzacions ja des de la nit abans, amb l’objectiu de “fer entendre al proper govern estatal que la classe treballadora pot parar el país”. Més seguretat a les vies (10 i 12 de novembre) Després del tràgic accident d’Urda , amb la mort de 69 persones, el sindicat majoritari de maquinistes, Semaf, ha convocat una vaga per als dies 10 i 12 de novembre —just abans i després de la vaga general— per reclamar mesures de seguretat . En concret, per al 10, el sindicat preveu una aturada total del servei al grup Renfe, mentre que el dia 12 les aturades seran parcials al llarg de la jornada. Semaf crida a l’aturada després de constatar una “manca de compromís real amb la seguretat” dels responsables del transport ferroviari. Millores laborals a la indústria càrnia (9-13 de novembre) La indústria càrnia ha convocat vaga entre el 9 i el 13 de novembre pel bloqueig de la negociació del conveni estatal . L’objectiu dels sindicats és pressionar les patronals perquè acceptin les millores en matèria salarial i de condicions, especialment de reducció de la jornada . La convocatòria afectarà escorxadors, sales de desfer, fàbriques d’elaboració d’embotits i serveis auxiliars d’inspecció veterinària. El sector carni és un dels principals motors de la indústria agroalimentària a Catalunya i ocupa a uns 30.000 treballadors , principalment a les comarques de Girona, Lleida, Osona i el Bages. Els metges estan en vaga indefinida des de dimecres passat , mentre que els mestres van fer diverses concentracions a les portes dels centres educatius dijous. Coincidint amb l’11-N, sindicats com la USTEC criden a la mobilització i avisen: “Sense casa no hi ha educació”. A més, els mestres tenen prevista una manifestació educativa el 21 de novembre i una vaga el 26 d’aquest mateix mes , tres dies abans de les eleccions generals. articles.body: Les conseqüències dels aiguats de principis d’octubre es continuen notant als barris de muntanya . Els veïns de Torre Baró , per exemple, lamenten que hi ha punts que segueixen pràcticament igual que després de l’episodi de pluges. És el cas del passatge de Carreras, on hi va haver una esllavissada , on es van col·locar tanques per frenar la caiguda de terra. Ara bé, Gabriel Raya, veí del carrer, creu que no és una barrera gaire efectiva, sobretot si uns aiguats de la mateixa intensitat es tornen a produir: “ No soc geòleg, però pot ser molt fàcil que torni a caure “. Uns metres mes enllà, al carrer de Sant Feliu de Codines, la pluja van provocar un esvoranc al marge de la calçada. Ara el forat està acordonat, però continua sense tapar. El Pablo Torrer, veí de la zona que hi passeja sovint, alerta: “Caurà fins i tot la casa que hi ha al costat”. A més, l’accident també impedeix que pel carrer hi circuli l’autobús de la manera habitual, perquè només un dels tres vehicles que fa la línia —el més petit— hi pot passar: “ Va un mes que estem sense autobús, com als anys 60 “. També et pot interessar Els barris de muntanya, els més damnificats per la pluja: esllavissades i un rescat de pel·lícula Marta de San Nicolás Núria Granados Ricard Cosialls 3 minuts de lectura Demanen celeritat a l’Ajuntament “ El veí ha d’arreglar el carrer? Ha de ser l’Ajuntament “, recalca Torrer, que assegura que han estat els mateixos veïns els qui han fet molts dels arranjaments. De fet, Raya explica que l’ajuda no va arribar fins al tercer dia i que qui va parar el cop va ser el veïnat: “El primer pas el vam fer nosaltres, perquè, si no, no podíem ni caminar pel carrer”. Un mes després de tot plegat, demanen celeritat en les actuacions municipals , però de moment diuen que no hi ha resposta del consistori. Se senten abandonats, però no és cosa nova: “És com si Torre Baró sempre anés a part”. articles.body: L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha aprovat inicialment el projecte de reurbanització de l’espai públic dels interiors d’illa que delimiten els carrers de Juan de Mena i Pare Mariana i el passeig de la Vall d’Hebron , al barri de la Vall d’Hebron. El projecte d’arranjament afecta una superfície total de més de 13.800 m² i té un pressupost de 8,4 M€. Les obres de remodelació s’iniciaran la primavera del 2027 i s’allargaran fins a finals del 2028. Es tracta d’una actuació a través de la qual es vol impulsar una millora urbana general i integral de tot aquest entorn per facilitar l’ accessibilitat i el pas dels vianants ; crear itineraris amb pendents més suaus, i generar llocs d’estada i esbarjo també per a la mainada, amb zones de jocs infantils , mobiliari urbà i reforç de la il·luminació del carrer . Sense cotxes ni places d’aparcament Per fer-ho possible, l’ eliminarà una zona d’estacionament de vehicles propera al passeig de la Vall d’Hebron: 35 places de cotxe i 31 places de motocicleta. A més, també es prohibirà el trànsit rodat dins de tot l’àmbit, excepte per a operacions de càrrega i descàrrega i per a vehicles d’emergència. La desaparició de la zona d’aparcament farà guanyar a l’entorn de 800 m² d’espai lliure i d’ús públic . Es suavitzaran els 15 metres de desnivell La millora de la mobilitat i la introducció d’elements d’accessibilitat és també un dels objectius destacats d’aquest projecte, ja que l’àmbit d’actuació té desnivells de fins a 15 metres . Fins ara aquest desnivell se salva amb escales i graons. El projecte planteja crear itineraris accessibles amb rampes més suaus que facilitin la mobilitat tant en sentit longitudinal com transversal, per eliminar barreres. També et pot interessar Barcelona invertirà més de 150 M € per fer zones verdes en espais en desús i per guanyar més ombra Maria Solans Sílvia Gutiérrez 4 minuts de lectura Adaptació al canvi climàtic Amb el projecte, es vol reconnectar aquest veïnat amb tot l’entorn, i alhora implantar una arquitectura més identitària, preservant aquells paviments i elements urbans que hi són propis. Aquesta actuació forma part del Programa d’espais de proximitat i interiors, una estratègia municipal emmarcada en el Pla clima que té com a objectiu incrementar i transformar els espais quotidians de la ciutat, posant l’accent en el verd, l’ombra, la renaturalització i l’adaptació al canvi climàtic. El projecte preveu mantenir i millorar la vegetació existent , molt abundant en aquest sector: es farà una revisió acurada de l’estat dels arbres i arbustos, per substituir els que no es trobin en bon estat, i s’hi incrementarà el verd . articles.body: El gènere fantàstic gaudeix de bona salut. Ho demostren les xifres del Festival 42 , que aquest diumenge tanca la sisena edició amb 8.100 assistents . Durant cinc dies —del 4 al 8 de novembre— la Fabra i Coats s’ha convertit en un espai de referència per als amants d’aquest gènere, i ha estat punt de trobada i debat entre autors i lectors. El festival ha reunit figures internacionals com Sequoia Nagamatsu, Elaine Vilar Madruga, Ken Liu i Mahmud El Sayed ; autors catalans destacats com Maite Carranza, Alicia Kopf o Laura Gost , i la participació de Cristina Fernández Cubas , flamant Premi Cervantes 2026 . També et pot interessar Cristina Fernández Cubas: “Cada conte és una aventura que comença de nou” Esther Castarnado 2 minuts de lectura Les pors contemporànies, protagonistes La programació d’aquest any ha estat marcada per les pors contemporànies , i com el gènere fantàstic és capaç d’interpretar la realitat actual i imaginar futurs possibles . Al festival s’hi han tractat qüestions com la crisi climàtica, l’accés a l’habitatge, la responsabilitat humana davant la intel·ligència artificial o els mecanismes de control i manipulació en l’era Trump. “Els gèneres fantàstics ens permeten parlar de qüestions que de vegades costa abordar des de la quotidianitat. El terror i la utopia ens ajuden a afrontar les nostres pors , a mirar des d’altres punts de vista i a generar empatia. La literatura fantàstica no és una fugida de la realitat, sinó una manera d’entendre-la i, alhora, d’imaginar que les coses poden ser diferents”, expliquen les comissàries de l’edició, Karen Madrid i Susana Vallejo. Lectors de totes les generacions Un cop més el festival s’ha caracteritzat per la diversitat de públics i ha aplegat lectors de totes les generacions , des d’adolescents fins a aficionats fidels al gènere. “Aquesta barreja és una de les grans riqueses del 42”, destaquen Vallejo i Madrid. Al festival hi han acudit més de 170 participants i ha tingut una programació amb 71 activitats , dues exposicions — com la del dibuixant de còmic català Albert Monteys —, una ruta literària, tallers, dues convencions temàtiques i diverses propostes escèniques. A banda, el certamen també volgut retre homenatge a Richard Matheson en el centenari del seu naixement, a Stephen King amb motiu dels 50 anys de l’adaptació cinematogràfica de Carrie i a Olga Xirinacs en el seu norantè aniversari.
